log_2(1)=0 is the positive-domain boundary anchor; log_2(32)=5.

cases.prompt: Compare log_2(3) and log_2(5); justify your comparison without relying on a decimal approximation
cases.boundaryOracle: For b>1 and positive inputs, argument order is preserved; 3<5 gives log_2(3)<log_2(5).

cases.prompt: Compare log_(1/2)(3) and log_(1/2)(5); justify your comparison without relying on a decimal approximation
cases.boundaryOracle: For 0<b<1, positive argument order reverses; x=1 gives log_b(1)=0. The opposite ordering at b>1 must be rejected as a different base case.

cases.prompt: Compare log_4(3) with log_2(3) using exact change-of-base reasoning. Then decide whether log_2(x)<log_3(x) holds for every x>0; justify your decision at x=1, 0<x<1, and x>1.
cases.expectedCanonical: log_4(3)<log_2(3); the universal claim log_2(x)<log_3(x) is false: x=1 gives equality, 0<x<1 gives <, and x>1 gives >
cases.acceptedEquivalent: log_4(3)=(1/2)log_2(3)<log_2(3) since log_2(3)>0; log_2(x)<log_3(x) only for 0<x<1, equals at x=1, reverses for x>1
cases.rejectWrongOrMalformed: log_4(3)>log_2(3) and log_2(x)<log_3(x) for all x>0
cases.boundaryOracle: For x=3, log_4(3)<log_2(3). For log_2(x) vs log_3(x), x=1 gives equality, x>1 gives >, and 0<x<1 gives <; a universal fixed comparison is false.

coder8TypedPracticeCandidate.automaticScope: closed relation choices only; mathematical justifications ALWAYS human-scored with L06 rubric

cases.boundaryOracle: Domain requires x>3; x=3 is excluded even before solving, and x=5 is valid.
Base=1 is invalid even when the argument is strictly positive.
Negative real logarithm arguments are excluded; a negative logarithm VALUE may be valid.
Argument zero is excluded; log_b(x) tends toward a limit but is not defined at x=0.
Nonpositive bases are invalid as real logarithm functions, independent of argument.
Product law applies to positive products, not sums; log_2(2)+log_2(4)=3 but log_2(6)!=3.
Proof must use x,y>0,b>0,b!=1 and inverse exponents, not a decimal example.
The exact quotient and log_2(7) are equivalent; reject x=7/2 and check 2^x=7.
The inverse identity requires argument 7>0 and valid base 2; 2^(log_2(0)) is invalid.
